clue.text: Old bouncer somehow becomes a distinguished chef

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unspecified route, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A retired nightclub doorman unexpectedly reinvents himself as a top chef.
explanation.definitionFit: A cordon bleu is a cook of the highest class, named after a French order's blue ribbon.

clue.text: Plan to study steeple

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a spire is the pointed top of a steeple

explanation.surface: Someone intends to examine a church steeple.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot or scheme together, a verb sense of plan.

clue.text: Victim in genuine denial

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters of the other

parts.note: genuine means real
the butt of a joke is its victim

explanation.surface: A real victim is genuinely in denial about what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction or refutation, so a form of denial.

clue.text: Music hall act seen from circle, thrilled more when broadcast (unknown number)

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A theatregoer in the dress circle enjoys a variety act more when it is on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Mother Riley was a drag character played by Arthur Lucan in British music halls, films and radio from the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish washerwoman character was one of the best-known turns of British variety theatre.

clue.text: Simple when described by writer

indicators.note: to describe a figure is to draw a line around it, so one word is encircled by another

parts.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Something counts as simple when an author puts it into words.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and simple both describe something elementary, without complication.

clue.text: Explain cryptic clue, one on fruit

indicators.note: cryptic means obscured, so the word is to be decoded into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one
the date is the fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: A solver is asked to explain a tricky crossword clue about a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make clear or throw light on something, a synonym of explain.

clue.text: Very quickly take a shine to private

parts.note: to take a shine to someone is to like them
a private matter is nobody's business but one's own

explanation.surface: An army private very quickly becomes fond of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to an extraordinary degree, often of speed: working like nobody's business is working very fast.

clue.text: Peninsula in part of Russia, top hidden from view

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, and hiding it removes it from the word

parts.note: Siberia is the vast Asian part of Russia

explanation.surface: A peninsula lies in a region of Russia whose summit is obscured.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula holds Spain and Portugal; Iberia is its classical name.

clue.text: Mock some footballers at Zagreb

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Fans jeer some players at a match in the Croatian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means imitation, and ersatz means a substitute or fake.

clue.text: Actor judging his role critically

indicators.note: a critical reworking of something takes it apart, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A performer assesses his own part with a critic's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Gielgud was a celebrated English stage and screen actor, famed for Shakespeare.

clue.text: See 6
One tucking in atop refurbished terrace

indicators.note: tucking in means putting something snugly inside something else
refurbished means done up anew, so the word is remade in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sits eating on top of a newly done-up terrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved outdoor area beside a house, much like a terrace.

clue.text: Punch shared in overpriced nightclub

parts.note: a clip round the ear is a blow
a joint account is shared

explanation.surface: Bowls of punch are shared out at a pricey club.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip joint is slang for a bar or club that overcharges its customers.

clue.text: Go with Rhoda nervously, a menace behind the wheel

indicators.note: nervous movement is jittery and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious passenger rides with Rhoda, a terrible driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A road hog is a selfish driver who takes up more than their share of the road.

clue.text: Prospector's mongrel I shot across entrance to diggings

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so one part goes around another
shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A prospector's dog was shot near the opening of his mine workings.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold miner digs for gold, one kind of prospector.

clue.text: For pain, see expert going round hospital

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so one word is placed around another

parts.note: an ace is an expert
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient in pain is told to see a specialist doing hospital rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Scottish sculptor spoils vestibule

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a hall is an entrance vestibule

explanation.surface: A Scottish artist's work ruins an entrance lobby.
explanation.walkthrough: William Calder Marshall was a Victorian sculptor born in Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs to William Calder Marshall, an Edinburgh-born Victorian maker of statues.

clue.text: Poet, one free from stress around New York

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the remainder goes outside another piece
free from means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: tension is stress
the Roman numeral for one, which is removed
the standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A poet escapes the pressures of life in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from the word for stress, then wrap what is left around NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was the Victorian Poet Laureate.

clue.text: Said hourly, when husband's not there

indicators.note: not there means absent, so the letter standing for husband is dropped

parts.note: horal is an old adjective meaning of the hours or hourly
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Something is said every hour while the husband is away.
explanation.walkthrough: HORAL is a rare dictionary word for hourly; take off its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, the adjective sense of said.

clue.text: Fix cut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fix firmly, as in the mind or memory
second meaning: to cut a design into a hard surface

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a repair instruction; the two words are separate meanings of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engraved on the memory is fixed there, and engraving metal means incising lines into it.

clue.text: Sergeant major undermines rising attacks

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the whole phrase reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for sergeant major
to sap a wall is to undermine it

explanation.surface: A sergeant major subverts an uprising of attackers.
explanation.walkthrough: Join the two pieces as a phrase, sergeant major then undermines, and turn the whole thing upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasms are sudden fits or seizures, as in attacks of coughing.

clue.text: Mysterious artist set up murderer, reportedly

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means turned to read upwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so a word is given by its sound

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis

explanation.surface: A shadowy painter is framed for murder, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means known only to a few, secret or mysterious.

clue.text: Fruit for each boy around end of term

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside a letter

parts.note: a boy's name

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boy gets a piece of fruit for the last day of school term.
explanation.definitionFit: The persimmon is an orange fruit also called sharon fruit or kaki.

clue.text: Indian leader, he raised game after noon

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means lifted to read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upwards
RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: An Indian statesman lifted his game in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of independent India.

clue.text: Sense changes in a city in the Ruhr valley

definitions.text: a city in the Ruhr valley

indicators.note: changes means is altered, so the letters move into another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A visitor senses something changing in an industrial German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a major industrial city in Germany's Ruhr district.

clue.text: Treacherous person — one shouldn't meet with one on the Emerald Isle?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for a hidden betrayer

definitions.text: one shouldn't meet with one on the Emerald Isle?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally a reptile lurking in Ireland's green fields, which legend says St Patrick banished

explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is Ireland, famously free of snakes, so the literal creature is one nobody should come across there; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a false friend who lies in wait, like a hidden serpent.

clue.text: Favourite's backed for pace

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the word reads from right to left

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, with the 's kept as S

explanation.surface: Punters back the race favourite for its speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace taken in walking.

clue.text: Scale drawing of stadium works, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a sports ground is a stadium
a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: An architect draws up a plan of a stadium's construction work.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground plan is a drawing to scale of a building's layout at floor level.
